title: Arm Holdings
bodyHtml:
Investment Thesis

ARM Holdings is the royalty model that wins regardless of which chip architecture wins. ARM processor IP is embedded in essentially every smartphone, most data centre servers (growing rapidly), every connected IoT device, and increasingly in AI accelerators and robot controllers. IBM and ARM have a formal collaboration on dual-architecture hardware for AI workloads. NVIDIA Grace CPUs (ARM Neoverse V2) in GB200 NVL72 AI racks means ARM captures a royalty on every AI server sold with Grace. The royalty per chip increases with each architecture generation (ARMv9 carries higher royalties than v8). The risk is RISC-V open-source alternatives gaining momentum: real but slow-moving given ARM's ecosystem depth.

Future Tech Roadmap

2nm Process Node (TSMC N2) Confident 2025
Leading-edge silicon node; volume production 2025: TSMC N2, Samsung SF2
📈 Intel 18A is Intel's competing 2nm-class process. It uses ASML High-NA EUV and RibbonFET GAA transistors. Customer wins for Intel Foundry at 18A would be a significant re-rating catalyst: currently the market is pricing in low probability of Intel foundry success.
▼ #6 · 70% leader: TSM 99%
Humanoid Robot (Factory Deployment) Confident 2026
Humanoids performing real production tasks commercially: Tesla Giga 2026 target
📈 ARM processor IP is used in robot motor controllers, edge inference chips, and real-time control systems. ARM benefits from humanoid robot deployment through IP royalties without direct hardware risk.
▼ #3 · 50% leader: TSLA 82%
GPU Compute Cluster Confirmed Ongoing
Large-scale GPU arrays enabling parallel matrix ops for deep learning training
📈 AWS EC2 UltraClusters with NVIDIA H100/A100 are the infrastructure on which most AI training happens. Amazon is both a GPU customer (from NVIDIA) and a custom silicon competitor: a dual position that makes it uniquely exposed to the AI compute cycle.
▼ #3 · 80% leader: NVDA 90%
Autonomous AI Agent Confident 2025
AI that plans, uses tools, and executes multi-step tasks with minimal human input
📈 Palantir AIP is the leading enterprise platform for autonomous AI decision-making in defence, intelligence, and commercial operations. The combination of proprietary operational data and AI agent execution is the Palantir moat: it is very difficult to replicate the customer relationships and data integrations.
▼ #3 · 50% leader: MSFT 75%
AI Hardware ASIC (TPU/NPU/Trainium) Confirmed Ongoing
Custom silicon optimized for matrix multiply and AI inference
📈 AWS Trainium and Inferentia are designed to run Amazon's own AI workloads and compete with NVIDIA H100 for price-sensitive customers. Custom silicon reduces per-inference costs and improves AWS margins on AI workloads.
▲ LEADING · 90% vs AVGO 88% · GOOGL 82% · AMZN 80%
#6 · 70% leader: TSM 99%

Business & Fundamental Analysis

Financial Health & Profitability

Yes, highly profitable. ARM operates an asset-light IP licensing model with gross margins near 95% and operating margins exceeding 45%.

AI Monetization & Business Goals

ARM aims to drive higher royalty fees per chip by transitioning the global smartphone and server market to its v9 architecture (which charges double the royalty rate of older v8 cores).

  • NVIDIA Grace CPUs: Leveraging ARM architecture for next-gen AI superchips.
  • Windows on ARM: Ramping AI PCs (Copilot+ PCs) utilizing Qualcomm ARM-based Snapdragon processors.

Capital Expenditure (Capex) Concerns

As a pure IP licensor, ARM does not manufacture or design physical silicon, resulting in near-zero capital expenditures and very high FCF conversion rates.

Partnerships & Alliances

  • NVIDIA: Grace CPU integration.
  • Qualcomm, Apple, & MediaTek: Core architecture licensing partners.

Controversies & Headwinds

  • Qualcomm Litigation: Ongoing breach-of-contract lawsuit against Qualcomm over Nuvia CPU designs, presenting contract termination risks.\n
